p: Runtime inspection confirms that this H200 EP=2 configuration uses Mxfp4MoEMethod with the checkpoint's expert weights upcast to BF16 and MoeRunnerBackend.TRITON (local expert weight shape 16 × 5760 × 2880). These are not measurements of native FP4 expert compute. The default Triton configuration is used because an H200-specific E=16 tuning file is absent. Both target and draft communicate through NCCL AllReduce/AllGather.

The following granularity controls use 4k context, the same full-graph settings as the main sweep, and full completion dependencies. Coverage and communication-gap coefficient of variation (CV, standard deviation divided by mean; lower is more even) are averaged over the two ranks' per-cycle medians. The serial control uses the same composed graph with overlap disabled. Three timing repetitions provide a range, not a confidence interval; small differences should not be treated as decisive.

Four compute groups are selected. At B16 they raise paired draft-compute coverage to 76.7%, versus 21.5% averaged across ranks for the previous schedule. Draft compute spans about 99% of the paired graph and occupies all 10 time deciles, versus about 11% and 2 deciles previously. Draft communication-gap CV falls from about 0.555 to 0.242, with communication spread over about 79% of the pair. Eight groups slightly improve compute coverage but make communication spacing less even; 16 and 64 groups bring no useful improvement.

All seven full-completion controls have zero measured forbidden intersections on both ranks: target communication versus draft communication, draft communication versus draft compute, and target compute versus draft compute. Their 21 workloads / 1,764 timed token sequences exactly match the previous schedule's reference outputs. At B4/B16/B64, the selected four-group control reaches 374.1/977.9/2959.4 tokens/s, compared with 380.5/1018.5/3030.1 for the previous schedule. Better overlap therefore does not establish an end-to-end speedup.

An additional internal-PDL preservation variant is rejected: all six overlap/serialized workloads fail comparison with the previous schedule (419 of 504 timed sequences differ) and show unstable repeated outputs, although GSM8K sanity accuracy is 19/20. Its apparent throughput improvement is not a valid speedup. The public flag was removed; the failed variant remains reproducible at commit 46f0b5d29b and its traces are retained with the experiment evidence. CUDA programmatic dependencies can release a successor before its predecessor finishes; full completion dependencies remain the selected policy. The precise cause of the failed variant is not isolated.

Plots below show actual kernel intervals for a representative B16/4k verification-A + draft-B pair on rank 0. Communication intervals include NCCL execution/wait time, not a measurement of wire-transfer time. They exclude the rest of the decode iteration, and kernel interval union avoids double-counting simultaneous kernels.
CUDA dependency reference: NVIDIA CUDA 13 programming guide.
